title: Chimera Deploy Orchestra: mini-manifest and release notes (draft)
body:
Context:
This is a compact, operational-first checklist and hour-by-hour mini-manifest for the Chimera deployment (small feature set + routing changes). Purpose: coordinate a low-risk, telemetry-driven canary, with a rapid backfill/rollforward path and clear release notes for customer-facing comms.

High-level objectives:
- Push feature flags F-CHI-1..F-CHI-4 behind network routing flip.
- Validate model-routing fallback for eu-west region (route policy V2).
- Keep p95 latency delta < 20% vs baseline.
- No customer-impacting errors; any 5xx > 0.5% in 30m triggers rollback.

Release window (local times are UTC):
- Tue 2028-01-17 09:00 — preflight signoff (30m)
- Tue 2028-01-17 09:30 — deploy chimera control-plane + config (10m)
- Tue 2028-01-17 09:45 — start micro-canary (1% traffic)
- Tue 2028-01-17 10:15 — expand canary to 10% if signals green (15m observation)
- Tue 2028-01-17 10:45 — expand to 35% (30m observation)
- Tue 2028-01-17 11:30 — full rollout to 100% (gradual ramp over 45m)
- Tue 2028-01-17 12:30 — post-rollout stabilization check (60m)
- Tue 2028-01-17 13:30 — release notes publish (internal->external)

Preflight checklist (owners in parens):
- Merge PRs and tag release build: runtime PR #678 merged (Samira)
- Build artifacts verified (sha256) and uploaded to registry (Diego)
- Infra smoke infra job green in staging (Ethan)
- Canary traffic script prepared (local load generator + synthetic user set) (Maya)
- Metrics dashboard pinned and shared: latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, traffic, kv-cache hit-rate (Priya)
- Alerts tuned for this window (SLO guardrails): p95 > baseline*1.2, 5xx > 0.5% (SRE)
- Pager rota confirmed for 09:00–14:00 UTC (oncall list in Slack #deploys)

Micro-canary runbook (step-by-step):
1) 09:30 — Deploy control-plane config: apply config v2-routing (10m). Verify config rollout via /admin/config (expected: all replicas show v2).
2) 09:40 — Kick micro-canary: set route-weight for chimera-lane to 1% in traffic-router.
3) 09:40–09:55 — Observe: key signals (fresh request trace check list):
   - Latency: p95 < baseline*1.2
   - Errors: 5xx < 0.5%
   - Token cost variance: < 10%
   - KV-cache warmup trend: hit-rate trending upward
   - Model fallback success: 100% of intentional fallback tests succeed
4) 09:55 — Decision: proceed or abort. If any signal fails -> immediate rollback: revert route-weight to 0% and revert config (Rollback steps below). Notify #deploys.
5) 10:15 — If green, scale to 10%: update traffic-router and incrementally add canary workers (new autoscale group).
6) 10:15–10:30 — Observe 15m; run smoke prompt set (see linked artifacts).
7) 10:45 — If green, expand to 35% and monitor 30m.
8) 11:30 — If green, initiate 100% ramp in 10% increments every 10m with rapid checks after each increment.

Rollback/abort quick-steps (fast path):
- Runbook quick command: /scripts/deploy-revert chimera v2
- Revert traffic-routing: set chimera-lane weight to 0%
- Toggle feature flags OFF: F-CHI-1..4 -> off (feature-flags service)
- Re-run baseline health checks and open incident in Jira INF-2137-rollback
- Notify: page primary oncall, post summary in #deploys and #customers-impact (if customer effects seen)

Smoke/validation prompts (automated + manual):
- Small curated set (synth-chi-01..05) that exercise model fallback, streaming window, and kv-cache hot-path. Results recorded to S3 prefix s3://ci-artifacts/chimera/smoke/2028-01-17
- Manual quickchecks: 5 chat interactions (Maya), 10 embedding calls (Priya), 3 long-seq generation stress calls (Ethan)

Observability anchors and diagnostic tasks:
- Dashboards: chimera-canary-summary (pinned), control-plane-sync, downstream-queue-depth, model-inference-latency
- Traces: sample 100 traces for canary requests every 15m; attach to PR/incident if anomalies
- Logs: grep for "permission denied" and "model fallback" occurrences; surface top 5 error messages
- Cost telemetry: token-per-response distribution; check quantization path differences

Post-rollout stabilization checklist:
- 30m rolling window validation: error-rate < threshold, p95 stable
- Verify autoscaling behaved as expected (no hot pods, no OOMs) (Diego)
- Confirm canary KV-cache hit-rate returned to baseline (Priya)
- Mark feature flags to permanent if stable (product signoff)
- Tag release and update CHANGELOG draft

Draft release notes (internal -> external staging):
Title: Chimera: safer routing rollouts and minor feature toggles\Summary:
- What: Gradual rollout of a routing policy update (v2) that enables more robust model fallbacks and a set of small feature toggles to improve routing resilience.
- Why: Reduce customer-visible latency spikes when primary nodes experience transient load and enable smoother fallbacks to warm KV-cached paths.
- Impact: No expected user-facing changes. Behavior change limited to internal routing and fallbacks; we will monitor latency and error rates closely during rollout.
- Rollout: Gradual canary starting 2028-01-17 UTC; full rollout targeted the same day if green.
- Known limitations: This rollout does not change model weights or core model binaries. Some internal metrics may show transient increase in token cost during warmup windows.

Customer-facing note (short):
We’re deploying a routing improvement to make fallbacks more reliable. If you see any latency regressions, please open a support ticket referencing "Chimera rollout".

Open questions / TODO (needs triage before publish):
- Confirm SLO escalation wording with legal/comms (Maya) — are we comfortable publishing the 0.5% error threshold?
- Should we include an opt-out flag for enterprise customers on Private deployments? (sales/solutions engineering)
- Finalize list of telemetry retained for 30 days vs 90 days for this experiment (security/compliance)

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Jenkins: job/chimera-build/lastSuccessfulBuild (artifact download)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/678
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-2137 (epic), INF-2137-1..3 (rollforward tasks)
- Slack: #deploys (primary), #sre-oncall (escalation), #customers-impact (external comms)
- Rollback script: /ops/bin/chimera-rollback --reason \"auto-detect\"

Notes to self: quick telemetry thresholds set in dashboard are intentionally permissive for the first 15 minutes to avoid noisy aborts; tighten after 30m. Keep a 1:1 ops shadow for the first 90 minutes to speed remediation.

End of mini-manifest.
